transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-02
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (NexaHealth Eng Lead), Maya Thompson (NexaHealth PM), Sam Patel (NexaHealth Security)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're on for the weekly POC sync. quick roll call?
[00:04] Jordan Reyes: yep Jordan here.
[00:06] Maya Thompson: Maya here.
[00:07] Sam Patel: Sam.
[00:08] Priya Singh: Priya here. thanks.
[00:10] Alex Chen: cool. quick agenda - onboarding status, environment readiness (vpc peering, sso, kms), quick review of the benchmark results you ran last week, tuning suggestions, and then next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Jordan Reyes: yes, sounds good.
[00:20] Alex Chen: great. Jordan, can you kick off with a quick update on what you did since last week?
[00:25] Jordan Reyes: yeah so we got environment access partially set up. we created the staging VPC and we tried the initial peering test but hit a routing issue, uh the peering connection was established but the subnets weren't routing to the redwood side. we think it's a route table entry missing. also we spun up an internal test node to generate traffic, about 10 qps for the latency tests.
[00:46] Priya Singh: mm-hmm, that matches what we saw from the logs - the connection attempt reached our gateway but we never saw the client traffic reach the inference pool. likely a route table / security group egress rule.
[00:58] Maya Thompson: quick Q on the SSO side, we tried SAML with our okta test account, but the SSO redirect error'd. is that something we need to set in the console or is it on our side?
[01:10] Alex Chen: good question. typically we need the SP metadata from your Okta config; Priya can share the exact redirect/callback URL. sometimes transcription errors on my part - that url shows up weird in the console - but it's usually a missing ACS url or time sync issue.
[01:24] Priya Singh: yes, I'll paste the ACS/callback URL into the chat after the call I'll also include the cert thumbprint example.
[01:31] Sam Patel: on the security checklist, team wants clarity on KMS/HSM we need to know if keys stay in our KMS, what access Redwood engineers have, and key rotation support. we sent the compliance questionnaire earlier.
[01:44] Alex Chen: understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS; by default keys can stay in your cloud KMS and we integrate with it via IAM roles and limited access. for the POC we can demonstrate a flow where you hold the key and we never see plaintext. Priya, can you confirm the HSM rotation options?
[01:59] Priya Singh: yep, we support customer KMS and we can do envelope encryption. rotation is supported but for the demo we usually show the key usage logs in the customer's KMS console; Redwood will only have a service role that can call decrypt ops with your explicit IAM allow. we'll include the diagram in the doc pack.
[02:20] Jordan Reyes: great. on benchmarks last Wednesday we ran the 1x baseline with the open model you recommended (redwood-1-small, uh sometimes the name shows weird in doc). results: avg p50 latency ~135ms at 10 qps with burst to 20 qps, p95 ~320ms, throughput plateaued at around 18 tokens/sec per GPU. cost looked ok but we're hoping to get p50 below 100ms for user-facing flows.
[02:48] Alex Chen: thanks. quick note we sometimes show model name as redwood-1-sm vs redwood-1-small in logs, sorry for the confusion. the latency profile you saw suggests batch size maybe too small or KV cache not primed. did you run with prefix caching enabled?
[03:03] Jordan Reyes: we left caching off for the baseline to keep it simple.
[03:06] Priya Singh: okay that's why. enabling prefix/KV cache should drop p50 significantly for repeated contexts. also increasing the batch target and using dynamic batching can help, there's a tradeoff with added latency for cold requests but for typical traffic patterns you should see lower p50 at similar cost.
[03:25] Maya Thompson: what's the recommended batch target for our QPS? we expect about 30 concurrent users during peak but each sends short prompts (~60 tokens).
[03:32] Priya Singh: for 10-30 qps with ~60 token prompts we usually recommend batch target 4-8 and adaptive batching windows ~20-40ms. run an experiment: 1x baseline, then 2x batch run compare p50/p95 and token cost. Alex, we offered to run a 2x batch test and share the spreadsheet?
[03:51] Alex Chen: yeah we'll run artifacted tests; but quickest is to have Jordan run it in staging with the new config Priya will provide the exact config flags. we can also run a controlled run on our side with same traffic profile to verify.
[04:04] Jordan Reyes: ok i'll try to run the 2x batch by end of week, but if you can also run on your infra that helps for apples-to-apples.
[04:11] Alex Chen: will do. Priya, anything on quantization or kernels?
[04:15] Priya Singh: yep for the model you picked there's a quantized path (int8) that reduces memory and improves throughput. small caveat: int8 can have minor quality drift on edge cases; we can run a quality regression test on your eval set. plus our runtime picks optimized kernels based on seq length; if your seqs are short (~60) we can choose kernels that favor latency. we'll include recommended compile flags.
[04:41] Sam Patel: about data retention and logs what logs do you store? audit logs? can we turn off request storage?
[04:48] Alex Chen: Redwood has configurable retention. for Private you control retention and can opt out of storing request payloads; we retain telemetry for ops but can scrub PII on ingest. for hosted mode there's retention defaults but enterprise tenants can request stricter policies. we'll share the exact retention table and the SOC2 doc.
[05:05] Sam Patel: perfect. also need to confirm whether Redwood engineers have access for troubleshooting we prefer jump-boxed access with session recordings rather than broad key access.
[05:14] Priya Singh: yes we use ephemeral, recorded sessions and role-based access for support. for the POC we'll supply the support runbook and who will request access.
[05:22] Maya Thompson: back to the routing issue Jordan said route table; do you have a quick checklist to verify from our side?
[05:28] Priya Singh: checklist: 1) ensure route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 or specific CIDR to the peering attachment, 2) security group egress allows outbound to Redwood's peering CIDR, 3) ensure NACLs aren't blocking, 4) if using private DNS ensure resolvers are correct. i can paste the snippet after call.
[05:46] Jordan Reyes: thanks, that will help.
[05:48] Alex Chen: cool. any blockers on the legal/procurement side? Maya?
[05:53] Maya Thompson: legal has some follow-ups on the DPA and liability clauses, but nothing blocking for the POC. procurement asked for a price cap for the POC so we can sign the form.
[06:04] Alex Chen: we can do a POC credit and cap i'll follow up with pricing details.
[06:09] Priya Singh: quick note on testing: if you want us to run a controlled benchmark we'll need the traffic profile and sample payloads; Jordan please share a replay or generator.
[06:19] Jordan Reyes: i'll upload a generator to the shared drive, link is in the chat it's a small jmeter-based script.
[06:25] Alex Chen: perfect. we'll run our 2x batch tests Monday and share the spreadsheet; Jordan try the 2x on your staging too.
[06:31] Sam Patel: going back to KMS can you confirm rotation cadence options? we require 90-day rotation in our policy.
[06:39] Priya Singh: we support rotation cadence down to 30 days; again keys live in your KMS so rotation is driven by your policy. we'll document the steps and show sample logs.
[06:49] Maya Thompson: ok great. any performance tuning suggestions beyond batch and cache?
[06:54] Priya Singh: yes 1) enable KV prefix caching for repeated contexts, 2) use quantized model path where acceptable, 3) reduce sequence length by truncation or templating to only necessary context, 4) pin model variants for canary fallback to smaller models if latency spikes. we can provide config examples.
[07:14] Jordan Reyes: about fallback does Redwood automatically route to cheaper models if we hit capacity? we want graceful degradation not failures.
[07:21] Alex Chen: yes, we support routing policies canary, fallback to smaller model, region-based fallback. we'll show a sample routing policy config in the rollout doc.
[07:31] Maya Thompson: last thing timeline: we aim to decide on Dedicated vs Hosted by end of Feb and production ready in April if all goes well. is that feasible?
[07:40] Alex Chen: timeline looks reasonable. decision end of Feb aligns with getting security review and benchmark sign-off. Dedicated procurement tends to take longer, but we'll support with pricing and capacity planning.
[07:50] Priya Singh: and for April prod we'd suggest a staged rollout with canary + automatic fallback.
[07:57] Alex Chen: alright let's recap next steps. we'll run the 2x batch benchmark and share spreadsheet (Alex), Priya to send VPC peering checklist and SSO ACS URL and terraform snippet, Sam to confirm KMS questions and we'll send SOC2 and retention docs, Jordan to run the 2x batch in staging and upload traffic generator. schedule next sync 2027-02-09.
[08:22] Jordan Reyes: thanks all.
[08:24] Maya Thompson: thanks.
[08:25] Sam Patel: thanks.
[08:27] Alex Chen: okay end meeting. references: benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://drive.company/benchmarks/nexaweek1), shared runbook (link: https://drive.company/runbooks/redwood-poc), compliance pack (link: https://redwood.docs/soc2)

Note: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts; speaker turns and timestamps approximated.
